main_body: Pink cherry-blossom tree: large round canopy (rows 0-31) on a short brown trunk (rows 32-41) with a small grass patch at the base
top_band: Organic canopy: lightest pink highlights mass across rows ~8-17 reads as the sunlit upper surface of the foliage, with darker pink/magenta on the lower canopy; no flat rim or band
evidence: Organic tree. The canopy is a volumetric blob lit from the top, with light pink on its upper and middle areas and darker magenta underneath, and the canopy casts a dark shadow over the trunk top. The trunk is a vertical face standing on a grass ellipse. It is not drawn as a flat elevation or a rim-only piece, and it reads as a 3/4 tree comparable to the references.

style.evidence: The canopy uses about 5 pink steps from deep magenta to near-white pink, with dithered clumps and speckle. The outline is a dark magenta-maroon tinted to the foliage rather than black. The trunk is a flat brown column with a lighter centre strip and little bark texture, and the grass patch has only 2-3 greens, so it is thinner than the reference trees, which have branches, root flares and many leaf clumps. The canopy silhouette is smooth and blobby, with less leaf-cluster definition than the reference. Still, an artist would probably accept it next to the reference.
